1.
Heard learned counsel for the applicants and learned Aga for the State and perused the record.

2.  This application under Section 482 Cr.P.C. has been preferred against the order dated 04.12.2023, passed by learned Additional District and Sessions Judge, Court No.7, Shahjahanpur in Session Trial No.549 of 2018 (State Vs. Ratiram and others), arising out of Case Crime No.201 of 2018, under Sections 498A, 304B I.P.C. in option 302/34, 201 I.P.C. and Section 3/4 D.P. Act,
Police Station- Mirzapur, District- Shahjahanapur, whereby the application moved on behalf of applicants-accused under Section 311 Cr.P.C. for recalling of P.W.1 Omkar Singh has been rejected.

sentences.text: 3. Learned counsel for the applicants submitted that applicants are accused in the aforesaid case.

In cross-examination of P.W.1 Omkar Singh, certain important questions could not be asked from him Ratiram And 2 Others vs State Of U.P. And Another on 13 August, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/149342370/
1 and thus, an application under Section 311 Cr.P.C. was moved for recalling of P.W.1 Omkar Singh for further cross-examination.

entities.text: Ratiram And 2 Others vs State Of U.P. And Another
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: In the said application, the questions to be asked were also mentioned.
It was submitted that the trial Court has rejected the said application in an arbitrary manner without considering facts of the matter.
It was stated that applicants may be granted one opportunity for cross-examination of P.W.1 Omkar in order to ask certain questions, which were mentioned in the application.
Learned counsel submitted the impugned order is liable to be set aside.
4. Learned AGA has opposed the application and submitted that there is no illegality or perversity in the impugned order.
The said session trial is pending since the year 2018.
The trial Court has rejected the application of accused persons by a reasoned order.
5. I have considered rival submissions and perused record.
6. Fair trial is the main object of criminal procedure and it is the duty of the court to ensure that such fairness is not hampered or threatened in any manner.

Fair trial entails the interests of the accused, the victim and of the society, and therefore, fair trial includes the grant of fair and proper opportunities to the person concerned, and the same must be ensured as this is a constitutional, as well as a human right.
The rules of procedure that have been designed to ensure justice are scrupulously followed, and the court must be zealous in ensuring that there is no breach of the same.

7. As far as question of jurisdiction under section 311 Cr.P.C. is concerned, it is clear that Section 311 Cr.P.C. empowers the court to summon a material witness, or to examine a person present at "any stage" of "any enquiry", or "trial", or "any other proceedings" under the Cr.P.C., or to summon any person as a witness, or to recall and re-examine any person who has already been examined if his evidence appears to it, to be essential to the arrival of a just decision of the case.
Undoubtedly, the Cr.P.C. has conferred a very wide discretionary power upon the court in this respect, but such a discretion is to be exercised judiciously and not arbitrarily.
The power of the court in this context is very wide, and in exercise of the same, it may summon any person as a witness at any stage of the trial, or other proceedings.
The court is competent to exercise such power even suo motu
if no such application has been filed by either of the parties.
However, the court must satisfy itself, that it was in fact essential to examine such a witness, or to recall him for further examination in order to arrive at a just decision of the case.

8. In the instant matter, it appears from record that after cross-examination of P.W.1 Omkar Singh was over, an application was moved under Section 311 Cr.P.C. for recalling of said witness, which was earlier rejected by the trial Court and thereafter in pursuance to order passed in application under Section 482 Cr.P.C. No.5783/2023 by this Court, P.W.1 Omkar Singh was recalled and his further cross-examination was conducted on 05.07.2023.

After that the applicants-accused have again filed the application under Section 311 Cr.P.C. for recalling of P.W.1 Omkar Singh for putting certain questions in cross-examination, which was rejected by the trial Court vide impugned order dated 04.12.2023.
It is apparent from facts of the matter that sufficient opportunity has already been granted to the accused persons for cross-examination of P.W.1 Omkar.
The trial Court has observed that the said application was moved in order to delay the trial.
The application of applicants has been rejected by a reasoned order.

Considering all relevant facts of the matter, it Ratiram And 2 Others vs State Of U.P. And Another on 13 August, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/149342370/
2 cannot be said that the impugned order is suffering from any such material illegality or perversity so as to require any interference by invoking powers under Section 482 Cr.P.C.

sentences.text: The application under Section 482 Cr.P.C. lacks merit and thus, liable to be dismissed.
9. The application under Section 482 Cr.P.C. is dismissed.
